head.name: @fzlt/core
head.lead: The kernel: one loop, bounded work, and the page always comes back. It is the whole default export: one shared requestAnimationFrame for every engine on the page, a fixed 60 Hz step with a catch-up cap, auto-pause, bounded pools, the event ring, seeded random, settle and an fps cap for page interactions, and the ledger that gives the page back on destroy(). Every brick is its own subpath.

items.doc: Make an engine: a fixed-step loop on the page's shared clock, with its own pools, event ring, seeded random and ledger. Add systems with add(), then start(); destroy() (or aborting o.signal) stops it and gives the page back.

items.doc: Records every change the engine makes to the page (styles, attributes, classes, text, added nodes) so restore() puts it back exactly. Writes that change nothing touch nothing, and an edit the host page made after ours always wins. Each engine has one: engine.ledger.

items.doc: A bounded pool. Every item is made up front, so acquiring and releasing never allocates and the pool never grows: when it's full, acquire() returns undefined (refuse new work).

items.doc: Seeded random (the DOM VIRUS core LCG, same sequence). Use it for anything that changes the simulation, so a run can be replayed or synced; state reads and restores it for snapshots. The state lives in a Uint32Array so drawing a number never allocates.
